topic: Support Ticket AI Reply Boundary Card: 7 Checks Before Automating Helpdesk Responses
boundary: Educational operations guide only — not legal, compliance, security, support-SLA, customer-result, revenue, savings, refund, incident-resolution, ranking, certification, or guaranteed-performance advice.

checks.owner_question: Is this a routine question, refund dispute, outage, access problem, data request, bug, complaint or legal/compliance issue?
checks.safe_action: Let AI draft only low-risk replies; route risky tickets to the named human owner.

checks.owner_question: Which help article, policy, order record, incident note or product owner update supports the reply?
checks.safe_action: Do not answer from memory or model confidence when the current source is missing.

checks.owner_question: Could the reply expose credentials, payment data, health/legal details, customer records, logs or another customer’s information?
checks.safe_action: Mask sensitive details and ask for secure-channel handling before sharing records.

checks.owner_question: Does the wording promise a refund, fix date, SLA credit, legal position, security outcome or future feature?
checks.safe_action: Use bounded status language and require owner approval for commitments.

checks.owner_question: What words or conditions force handoff: angry customer, chargeback, outage, repeated failure, data deletion, account lockout or regulated request?
checks.safe_action: Make stop rules visible inside the helpdesk workflow before automation is enabled.

checks.owner_question: Who reviewed the reply pattern, when, and what evidence link shows approval?
checks.safe_action: Keep an approval register for templates, macros, AI prompts and high-risk examples.

checks.owner_question: Which AI drafts were edited, rejected, escalated or caused follow-up confusion?
checks.safe_action: Feed review findings into updated templates, source articles and routing rules.

safe_scope: Uses ticket-risk classification, source-of-truth verification, sensitive-data masking, commitment boundaries, escalation stop rules, human approval records and weekly failure review; no legal, compliance, security, support-SLA, customer-result, revenue, savings, refund, incident-resolution, ranking, certification or performance guarantees.
